messages:
Maya (PM): Hey all — iterating on the Autoscale & Capacity panel. New goals: clearer capacity units, explicit burst controls (cap + duration), GPU pool chooser with search, SLO slider with numeric input, and visible guardrail types. Dropping the latest screens: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/autoscale-v2. PTAL — design review Friday.
Alex (Design): Quick visual notes: group min/max under 'Base capacity' and label as 'GPUs'. Use a pill for the burst toggle with 'Burst pool' when on. For guardrails, show inline examples (e.g., "block if p95 > 300ms").
Priya (Frontend): a11y checklist: slider must announce value and unit via aria-live when moved; numeric input should be reachable via tab order before the slider; color alone shouldn't convey soft vs hard. Also ensure focus outlines aren't removed.
Diego (Infra): Backend constraints: when burst is enabled we either map to an existing pool or provision a logical burst pool. Prefer decoupled logical pool (so quota & billing are separate). API proposal snippet: 

```
{"capacity": {"min_gpus": 2, "max_gpus": 10, "burst": {"enabled": true, "pool_id": "pool-burst-1", "cap": 4, "duration_mins": 30}}, "slo": {"metric": "p95_latency_ms", "target": 150}, "guardrails": [{"id":"g1","type":"soft","metric":"p95_latency_ms","threshold":200},{"id":"g2","type":"hard","metric":"error_rate","threshold":0.05}]}
```

Alex (Design): Love the API shape. Copy tweak: change 'cap' -> 'Burst capacity (GPUs)'; change 'duration_mins' label to 'Burst duration (mins)'. For the SLO control, show both slider and small input labeled 'p95 target (ms)'.
Sam (Eng Manager): Telemetry ask: emit events for edits + preview: `autoscale.update`, `autoscale.preview_cost`, `autoscale.guardrail_violation`. Add versions to diffs for rollbacks. Rollout: behind feature flag, start at 5% internal, then 25% customers.
Jordan (UXR): Usability test note: users confused by 'min/max instances' vs 'GPUs'. Let's surface examples: "Minimum capacity (GPUs) — e.g., 2 GPUs = 16 tokens/s baseline". Also test if 'burst' needs confirmation modal (billing implications).
Priya (Frontend): Implementation notes: I'll build a composite component: NumericInput + Slider + aria-hidden SVG gauge for screen readers. We'll need keyboard shortcuts: arrow keys adjust slider by 1, shift+arrow by 10. Also will add an autosuggest for GPU pool search; fallback to grouped dropdown if no match.
Diego (Infra): Ops & guardrails: soft = emit event + annotate request with warning; hard = reject scaling that would violate policy. We'll need a small policy service to evaluate guardrails in the control plane. Also: capacity presets map to saved policy bundles; good for quick rollouts.
Alex (Design): Color/contrast: soft yellow (#F5A623) and hard red (#D0021B) pass AA on white? double-check. If not, add icon + label. Also add tooltip copy: 'Soft guardrail: warns the team. Hard guardrail: blocks scaling actions.'
Maya (PM): Action items: @Priya mock keyboard + screenreader flows and attach a brief a11y checklist. @Diego share API PR for burst pool & guardrail service by EOD. @Sam outline telemetry schema and rollout plan. @Alex update Figma with copy tweaks and a small cost preview tile (estimate per hour). We'll reconvene Friday design review.
autoscale-bot: feature-flag "autoscale-panel-v2" toggled -> staging:true.
Priya (Frontend): I'll open a draft PR for the slider component (aria tags + numeric input) and add tests for keyboard interactions. ETA: Tue.
Diego (Infra): Posted API proposal: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/-/merge_requests/245. It includes guardrail evaluation API and burst pool lifecycle.
Sam (Eng Manager): I'll draft alerts for 'guardrail health'—counts of soft warnings and hard rejections per 5m, and a weekly digest. Need SLO target defaults for new customers.
Jordan (UXR): I'll schedule two quick moderated sessions next week to test language around 'burst' and 'presets'. Prefer weekday mornings.
Maya (PM): Thanks all — I'll update the RFC with these notes and add 'save as preset' UI copy examples ('Low-cost', 'Balanced latency', 'Max throughput'). See you Friday. :raised_hands:
